title: The Tower of Babel
lead: The story of humanity building a city and tower in Shinar, and God scattering them by confusing their language (Genesis 11:1–9). It explains the many languages of the world and sets up God's call of Abram; Christians read Pentecost (Acts 2) as its answer.

sections.b: Babel is the Hebrew name of Babylon, and the story sets up the long biblical contrast between God's purposes and Babylon's pride: Nebuchadnezzar's boast (Daniel 4:30), Isaiah's taunt over the king who wanted to climb to heaven (Isaiah 14:13–15), and "Babylon the great" in Revelation 17–18. The scattering of the nations (Genesis 10–11) is followed at once by God's promise that all the families of the earth will be blessed through Abram (12:3). Zephaniah promises "pure speech" to the peoples (Zephaniah 3:9), and at Pentecost people of many languages hear one message (Acts 2:5–11), an echo noticed since the early church.
